posts.image_headline: Is it really the same drug?
posts.image_subhead: Compounded semaglutide ≠ FDA-approved Ozempic or Wegovy
posts.caption_base:
A lot of lower-cost GLP-1 telehealth plans use compounded semaglutide — made by a compounding pharmacy, not the original manufacturer. It's not the same FDA-approved product tested in the STEP and SURMOUNT trials, and the FDA has published specific concerns about unapproved GLP-1 drugs sold for weight loss. That doesn't automatically make it unsafe — but it does mean the clinical trial evidence doesn't transfer over automatically. Know which one you're actually being prescribed before you start.

We break down which of the 21 GLP-1 telehealth providers we track are branded, mixed, or compounded-primary — link in bio.

posts.image_subhead: Our #1 GLP-1 provider isn't a paid partner. Our #4 is.
posts.caption_base:
Found is one of our sponsored referral partners — we may earn a fee if you sign up through our link. It still scores 8.3/10 and ranks 4th of 21 GLP-1 providers, below Ro (9.3/10), which pays us nothing.

That's on purpose. Every CitedRx Score is built from the same five factors — evidence match, independent rating, insurance support, clinical support model, and regulatory standing — regardless of who's paying for the placement.

Full methodology in our bio link.

posts.image_subhead: CitedRx's #1-ranked GLP-1 telehealth provider, out of 21
posts.caption_base:
Ro prescribes predominantly FDA-approved branded GLP-1s — Wegovy, Zepbound, and Ozempic — the exact medications tested in the STEP and SURMOUNT trials. Add a dedicated prior-authorization team for insured members and a 4.4/5 U.S. News rating, and it's our top evidence-match score in the category.

Ro isn't a CitedRx referral partner — this review wasn't paid for or reviewed by Ro. Full review in bio.

posts.image_subhead: FTC + Utah AG sued Hims & Hers in July 2026
posts.caption_base:
Before you sign up for an ED or weight-loss telehealth subscription, here's something worth knowing: in July 2026, the FTC and the Utah Attorney General sued Hims & Hers Health, alleging a deceptive multi-step cancellation process and improper sharing of health data with advertisers. Hims disputes the claims, and the case is unresolved.

We still rank Hims #1 in erectile dysfunction (8.8/10, down from 9.1 before this came to light) — but we think you should know what you're signing up for before you do. Full breakdown in bio.

posts.image_subhead: Same thing, different words — legal in all 50 states
posts.caption_base:
Estrogen and progesterone aren't controlled substances, so licensed clinicians can evaluate and prescribe menopause hormone therapy remotely almost anywhere in the U.S. — no in-person visit required.

We've scored 9 menopause/HRT telehealth providers on evidence match, independent ratings, insurance support, and more. If you've been putting off looking into HRT because you assumed it meant a string of in-person visits, it might be easier than you think. Link in bio.

posts.image_subhead: Nationwide vs. ~10 states — here's what actually matters
posts.caption_base:
Both are real trans-specialty telehealth practices using an informed-consent model for gender-affirming hormone therapy. The biggest practical difference: QueerMed serves patients nationwide; QueerDoc is licensed in roughly 10 states.

If QueerDoc serves your state, it's a legitimate option with a broader scope (puberty blockers, legal transition consults, surgery referrals). If it doesn't, QueerMed is the closest like-for-like alternative. Full factor-by-factor comparison in bio.
